title: Input phase of the universal simulation
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean input and $k$ work tapes, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, let $n,T,t$ be natural numbers, and let $z$ be a finite Boolean word, with $t\le T$. Let $e$ be a register record satisfying $e.nc=n$, $e.z=|z|$, $e.i=t\,\mathrm{Str}(M,n,z,T)+k(2T+1)$, $e.q=0$ when $t=0$ and $e.q=e.i-\mathrm{Str}(M,n,z,T)$ otherwise, $e.lb=t\,\mathrm{Str}(M,n,z,T)$, and $e.ll=e.pa=e.pb=e.tmp=0$. For every natural input position $ps$, the counter program started at the input phase with label determined by $t=0$, registers $e.f$, input position $ps$, and any output word reaches the snapshot phase with label determined by $t=0$, registers obtained from $e.f$ by replacing $e.i$ by $e.i+|z|+n+2$ and $e.q$ by $0$ when $t=0$ or by $e.i+|z|+n+2-\mathrm{Str}(M,n,z,T)$ otherwise, and unchanged input position $ps$. During this computation it appends the encoded instruction bits for each index in the interval from $e.i$ up to but excluding $e.i+|z|+n+2$, in order, and uses at most $(|z|+n+2)(L_{\max}(M)+20)$ steps.
